courses.name: Bandon Dunes (Bandon Dunes Golf Resort)
courses.dataAsOf: Tournament-tee yardages and pars from the resort's official Bandon Dunes course page (read Nov 2026). Black/Green/Gold/Orange/Royal Blue per-hole yardages, handicaps and ratings from undated third-party scorecards (GolfPass, Greenskeeper.org, GolfingRecord, AllGolfHoles, Stymie) read Nov 2026; the official site's full multi-tee scorecard image could not be retrieved.

holes.note: Favor the left side off the tee.
holes.green: Large hump in the left-middle of the green; approach is best played from the right side.

holes.note: The prevailing wind is into the player and from the left, pushing shots short or right.
holes.green: Collection area right of the green is the common miss. The blog mentions a pot bunker short. Severely undulating.

holes.note: Described as the first real birdie chance; the landing area for the second shot can be blind from the fairway.
Dogleg right toward the ocean. Aim the tee shot at the bunker straight ahead; a low shot up the right is often best.
holes.green: An 'infinity' green set on the bluffs with breakers behind (Kidd). Deep bunkers guard the front-left.

holes.note: Split fairway; drive into the right half. Plays straight into the prevailing summer (north) wind and can be a three-shot hole.
holes.green: Framed by mounds on both sides.
Deep bunker left; a miss right leaves a manageable chip.

holes.note: The fairway is wider than it looks; favor the left, over an outcrop of beach grass.
holes.green: Effectively three-tiered; the pin position matters greatly.
A narrow front opening makes the green look smaller than it is. Hump at the front-left can feed balls toward the center.

holes.note: Pot bunkers sit in the center of the landing zone.
A drive right gives the shortest approach; the left gives the best angle. The second shot is blind.
holes.green: Shallow green.

holes.note: Plays long, straight into the summer wind. USGA championship tee is 469 (2020, 2022), against the official 452.
holes.green: Bunker right of the green. Slopes away from the player.

holes.note: Club selection is critical.
holes.green: Shallow, firm green. A sod-faced bunker guards short shots, native fescue rises behind, and the open approach is front-right.

holes.note: Reachable downwind; terrain on the right can leave awkward lies. The Tournament and Black tees are both 553.
holes.green: Deep collection area short of the green.

holes.note: Dogleg right; use a fairway bunker as the aiming line, and drives left give a better angle. Three bunkers pinch the wide fairway. Nearly drivable in calm air by cutting the corner.
holes.green: Shallow, elongated green behind a distant dune. Kidd enlarged a small pot bunker at the green's right corner into a large sand area.

holes.note: Favor the left. Usually plays into the wind; in a 20-30 mph headwind a bunted driver may be needed.
holes.green: Narrow, exposed green.

holes.note: A driveable par 4 downwind. Kidd suggests a 3-wood aimed long-left toward the 17th tee and warns that the slightest miss right loses the hole.
holes.green: Green on the cliff edge (rebuilt/'revised' per Kidd). Avoid attacking right-side pins.

holes.note: A drive down the left gives the best angle; the landing area narrows the farther you hit it, and a north wind pushes the ball right.
holes.green: Largest green on the property at about 80 yards front to back (Kidd); the official guide calls it the deepest green on the course.

holes.note: Dogleg right. Drive left, aiming at the top of the golf shop; the second shot is blind, so use the right edge of the clubhouse as a reference. The lodge sits behind the green.
holes.green: From the right side the green is hidden, and two bunkers block run-up approaches.

courses.name: Chambers Bay
courses.dataAsOf: Official scorecard printed 10/2025 (Golf ScoreCards, Inc.), linked from chambersbaygolf.com; retrieved 2026-11-02

greens.grass: Poa annua (sodded): four greens in 2017, the rest in fall 2018, reopened April 2019. Originally fine fescue with a little colonial bentgrass; the 2015 U.S. Open was played on fescue greens with 5-20% Poa contamination.

holes.name: Puget Sound
holes.note: Large landform and bunker up the right; partially blind second over a crest. 2015 U.S. Open: par 4 (496 yd) in R1, R3, R4 and par 5 (598 yd) in R2, swapping with No.
holes.green: Elevated green tight to a bank; drop-off left to short grass ~15 ft below; small bunker off the back; approach favours the right side.

holes.name: Foxy
holes.note: Knob in the landing area. Name references the 14th at Royal Dornoch (that page's body text spells it 'Roxy'). 2015 U.S. Open: 399 yd.
holes.green: Split by a large ridge; large bunker left, small bunker right; open entrance from the right. Falls right-to-left off the right side toward the big left bunker.

holes.name: Blown Out
holes.note: 2015 U.S. Open: 163-198 yd depending on the day.
holes.green: Kidney-shaped with a small ridge; deep bunker and deep fescue left; swale behind collects long shots; large kick slope on the right.

holes.name: Hazard's Ascent
holes.note: Immense bunker complex along the right off the tee. Played as a par 4 (495 yd) at the 2015 U.S. Open; par 5 (568 yd) at the 2010 U.S. Amateur.
holes.green: Large and heavily contoured; sand on three sides (front bunker running down the right, three blowout bunkers in the banks behind); natural backstop for long…

holes.name: Free Fall
holes.note: Fairway slopes left and narrows just past 300 yd; massive bunker complexes on both sides; semi-blind approach from the left.
holes.green: Deep pot bunker fronting the green; low chipping area behind. Severely back-to-front.

holes.name: Deception Point
holes.note: Partially blind tee shot; plays as a dogleg right or short and straight depending on tee. Lengthened ~100 yd for 2015, playing 495 yd.
holes.green: Long, narrow green perched between two bunkers and framed by dunes and long bunkers. Back-to-front.

holes.name: Humpback
holes.note: Bends right around a large bunker/waste complex on the right; aim left off the tee. Stroke index 1; operator calls it the hardest hole for all levels. 2015 U.S. Open: 508 yd.
holes.green: Elevated, multi-tiered: significant false front and a perpendicular ridge creating three shelves; two hummocks short-left block the view from the left.

holes.name: High Road Low Road
holes.note: In 2015 the only hole without a bunker. Hillside left, steep drop right; fairway slopes left-to-right. 2015 U.S. Open: 614 yd, the longest hole.
holes.green: Long and narrow with several ridges; contours left and back; area right of the green is blind.

holes.name: Olympus
holes.note: Tee is the course's high point.
holes.green: Oversized, one of the largest on the course; contours funnel balls toward the hole; large bunker short-right. Left-to-right.

holes.name: High Dunes
holes.note: Landing area narrows between dunes and sand; diagonal approach. 2015 U.S. Open: 436/468 yd.
holes.green: Relatively flat, tucked between dunes; deep bunkers front-right and back-left. Slopes away from the dunes.

holes.name: Shadows
holes.note: Dogleg left with a hillock/mound in the middle of the fairway (carry ~300 yd); hillside right, drop-off left. 2015 U.S. Open: 500/537 yd.
holes.green: Slightly elevated; ridge bisects it lengthwise; misplayed shots can roll ~40 yd away. Approach from the right. Right-to-left, falls down to the left.

holes.name: The Narrows
holes.note: Drivable par 4 and the narrowest hole; large blowout bunker short-left of the green.
holes.green: Largest green on the course (~12,700 sq ft), set in a punchbowl; long and skinny between two large mounds with distinct quadrants.

holes.name: Eagle Eye
holes.note: Dogleg right; widest fairway on the course (~115 yd) with a centreline bunker.
holes.green: Deep bunker in front; knob left of the green. Falls away on the right.

holes.name: Cape Fear
holes.note: Downhill tee shot over the course's largest waste area/bunker complex on the left, plus a centreline fairway bunker.
holes.green: Large, with a pronounced central ridge; back funnels balls away; collection area right; mound short-right. Tilts toward the front, then the back slopes away.

holes.name: Lone Fir
holes.note: The course's only tree (a Douglas fir) stands behind the green; fully exposed to wind off Puget Sound.
holes.green: Two-section green; the front repels poorly struck shots; well defended by waste bunkers. Left-to-right.

holes.name: Beached
holes.note: Short par 4, drivable from forward tees. Railroad and Puget Sound to the right; a long bunker/waste area runs the entire right side; fairway narrows just short of 300 yd.
holes.green: Smallest green on the course: tabletop, pear-shaped, about twice as wide at the front as the back; back tongue narrows to ~9 yd wide. ~50 yd deep.

holes.name: Derailed
holes.note: Long carry over a waste bunker and native area from the lower tee; the BNSF rail line runs the length of the right side, with Puget Sound beyond. 2015 U.S. Open: 172-218 yd.
holes.green: Split into two halves; right pins very hard to reach; bunker short-left; a long miss leaves a hard up-and-down. Middle tier slopes right-to-left.

holes.name: Tahoma
holes.note: Deep (~10 ft) cross bunker mid-fairway about 120 yd from the green; large bunker complex right. 2015 U.S. Open: par 5 (604 yd) in R1, R3, R4 and par 4 (525 yd) in R2.
holes.green: One of the largest and most severe greens. USGA describes four sections with the back-right hardest; GOLF.com describes three tiers. Bowl-shaped.

courses.name: Pebble Beach Golf Links
courses.dataAsOf: Current resort scorecard as listed by GolfPass (undated; Blue yardages match the pebblebeach.com course page, both checked 2026-11-02). Tournament setups: 2026 AT&T Pebble Beach Pro-Am (PGA TOUR), 2019 U.S. Open (AP), 2023 U.S. Women's Open (USGA).

greens.stimp: About 10 for resort play (Pebble Beach); 10.5 at the 2018 AT&T Pro-Am (GCSAA); faster than 12, settling at 13-15, for U.S. Opens (Pebble Beach).

holes.note: Dogleg right; tee shot is effectively a layup toward the corner fairway bunker, leaving ~150 yds in; trees block cutting the corner right.
holes.green: Elevated; bunkers on both sides. Tilts back-to-front toward the ocean.

holes.note: Par 5 for resort play, the AT&T Pro-Am and the 2023 U.S. Women's Open, but played as a 516-yd par 4 at the U.S. Open since 2000 (course par 71).
holes.green: Narrow green with a bunker along each side; the right bunker is the less forgiving.

holes.note: Severe dogleg left; long hitters can carry the trees on the left; second shot usually into the Pacific breeze.
holes.green: Slightly elevated with deep bunkers on both sides; Hale Irwin called it the hardest green to read in the world. Runs toward the ocean (right-to-left).

holes.note: Short par 4; tee shot must clear a cross bunker; driver can run just short of the green but brings the left bunker and the ocean right into play.
holes.green: Surrounded by bunkers; nine bunkers on the hole; 26 paces deep. Steeply pitched back-to-front; shots above the hole leave a hard putt.

holes.note: Jack Nicklaus-designed hole opened 1998. Safe play is left-centre.
holes.green: Shallow and wind-exposed; small bunkers in front, larger bunker back-left that cuts into the putting surface more than it appears.

holes.note: Penal bunkers down the left off the tee; tee re-angled toward Stillwater Cove in 2016. New back tee for the 2026 AT&T Pro-Am made it 540 yds (523 in 2025, +17).
holes.green: Hilltop green bunkered on both sides; one of five original 1919 greens.

holes.note: Shortest hole on the PGA TOUR; played 92 yds in the final round of the 2010 U.S. Open.
holes.green: Tiny green ringed by six bunkers; 'just over 20 yards deep'. Rebuilt 1992. Everything breaks toward the ocean.

holes.note: Aiming rock guides the tee shot from the lower tees; usually a 3-wood off the tee. Jordan Spieth played from the cliff edge in 2022, prompting the penalty-line change.
holes.green: 2022 restoration reclaimed 400 sq ft on an original 2,700 sq ft green (~3,100; Golf Digest says 'just over 3,000'); usable hole-location area more than doubled.

holes.note: Hardest hole at the 2019 U.S. Open. New 21-yd back tee for 2019 (526 yds). Fairway shaved toward the coastline for U.S. Open setup.
holes.green: One of the two smallest greens; 23 paces deep.

holes.note: Widest fairway on the course; three fairway bunkers punish left misses. A cliff-edge tee between the 9th green and the ocean was used in Feb 2021 (356 yds).
holes.green: On a bluff; bunkers catch misses long and left. Original 1919 green, restored and expanded in 2025 after shrinking to a few hundred sq ft of pinnable surface.

holes.note: Turns inland away from the ocean; fairway metal typical off the tee.
holes.green: Among the smallest greens; bunkers back and right. Measured 2,200 sq ft in 2019 but restored in 2021 to regain lost area; current size not published.

holes.note: Hard to hold when firm; best miss short-right except for front-left pins; trees on the right hide the wind.
holes.green: Wide but shallow; a large bunker guards most of the entrance. Original 1919 green. Shots finding the throat kick left toward the ocean.

holes.note: Bunker complex left of the fairway, three small bunkers right.
holes.green: Rebuilt 2017 adding ~400 sq ft on the right (Pebble Beach's 2019 summary says 300); restored left bunker sits ~6 ft below the surface.

holes.note: Dogleg right around trees with two large bunkers at the corner; among the hardest par 5s in championship golf; played over par at the 2019 U.S. Open.
holes.green: Elevated, walled off by a deep front bunker and a large false front that climbs halfway into the green; left side shaved.

holes.note: Lay up short of the mid-fairway pot bunker to leave under 125 yds.
holes.green: Well guarded; bunkers left. Slopes severely left, toward the unseen ocean.

holes.note: Tee shot must clear or avoid a mid-fairway island bunker, leaving ~150 yds in.
holes.green: Deep bunker short, small bunker long, trees left. Original 1919 green. Pitches sharply right-to-left.

holes.note: Usually plays into the Pacific wind; traditional Sunday U.S. Open pin is back-left.
holes.green: Hourglass/figure-eight shape; can play 15 yds longer or shorter depending on the pin with a massive front bunker and smaller bunkers long.

holes.note: Curves slightly right-to-left along the coast; tree in the fairway: drive left of it to reach in two, or right of it and lay up.
holes.green: Deep bunker right; towering pines left push play toward the ocean. Original 1919 green.

courses.name: Old Course at St Andrews
courses.dataAsOf: Everyday tees: St Andrews Links Trust Black/Blue/Green card as mirrored by GolfPass (accessed 2026-11-02; edition year not printed on the mirror). Championship: R&A card for the 150th Open (2022) plus R&A proposals (Oct 2025) for the 155th Open (2027).

greens.grass: Fescue (slender creeping red and chewings, overseeded spring and autumn) with browntop bentgrass; Poa annua also present. Cut to about 3.5-4 mm.
greens.stimp: About 9-9.5 ft for daily play; quickened to about 10-10.5 ft for The Open (course manager's figures, 2021). A 2010 reading was 9'8".

holes.name: Burn
holes.note: Shared fairway with the 18th, 129 yards wide (7.2 acres).
holes.green: Single green, no bunkers; fronted by the Swilcan Burn. Front half fairly flat; slopes and ripples at the back, with a back-left upper shelf.

holes.name: Dyke
holes.note: Gorse right; Cheape's bunker left, about 300 yds from the championship tee (2015). 2027: right-side fairway bunkers moved further down the hole.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 16th; two bunkers to the right of the green.

holes.name: Cartgate (Out)
holes.note: Bunker on the left of the fairway.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 15th; the Cartgate bunker cuts into the front-left. Vast, with subtle undulations and a counter-break.

holes.name: Ginger Beer
holes.note: Narrow fairway with mounds left and gorse right.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 14th; deep bunker left, hidden bunker right; Ginger Beer pot bunker behind.

holes.name: Hole O'Cross (Out)
holes.note: Seven bunkers right of the fairway; the Spectacles (two deep pots) sit about 50-60 yds short of the green. 2027: new championship tee.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 13th and the largest on the course; 37,846 sq ft is the whole double green.

holes.name: Heathery (Out)
holes.note: Blind tee shot; Coffin bunkers and hidden bunkers. 2027: new championship tee, road realignment and new left fairway bunker.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 12th; 104 yd is the width of the whole double green. No greenside bunkers.

holes.name: High (Out)
holes.note: The course's only true dogleg. Huge Shell bunker about 310 yds from the championship tee. 2027: new championship tee.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 11th; 112 yd is the width of the whole double green. Shell bunker guards the approach.

holes.name: Short
holes.green: Double green shared with the 10th; 36,063 sq ft is the whole double green. Short Hole pot bunker guards the front left.

holes.name: End
holes.note: Fairway bunkers right at about 260 and 290 yds (championship tee); gorse left. 2027: approach bunkers widened slightly.
holes.green: Single green; two bunkers in front, gorse close to the left. Few visual cues for judging distance. Relatively flat, tilting slightly from back left to front.

holes.name: Bobby Jones
holes.note: Narrow, undulating fairway; two small bunkers right at about 290 yds. 2027: new championship tee and new left fairway bunker.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 8th; 36,063 sq ft is the whole double green. Slopes front to back, falling away from a raised front, with subtle undulations.

holes.name: High (In)
holes.note: The original 'Eden' hole, fully exposed to wind off the estuary. 2027: championship tee extended.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 7th (112 yd is the whole green). R&A calls it probably the second-shallowest green after the 17th.

holes.name: Heathery (In)
holes.note: Short par 4 that long hitters can drive; several bunkers in the centre of the fairway are hidden from the tee, with gorse left and right.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 6th (104 yd is the whole green); prominent central pot bunker.

holes.name: Hole O'Cross (In)
holes.note: Coffin bunkers just under 300 yds from the championship tee; fairway ends around 300 yds.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 5th; 37,846 sq ft is the whole double green.

holes.name: Long
holes.note: Beardies bunkers left off the tee; the second shot must avoid Hell bunker (about 10 ft deep; its area is given as 300 sq m, 300 sq yd or 300 sq ft depending on the source).
holes.green: Double green shared with the 4th; sand surrounds the green. Steep front face, then falls away to the back and left; bulky dune shoulder at the front right.

holes.name: Cartgate (In)
holes.note: Fairway narrows around 300 yds; Sutherland bunker mid-fairway, with pot bunkers further up.
holes.green: Double green shared with the 3rd; pot bunker front left.

holes.name: Corner of the Dyke
holes.note: Principal's Nose (three bunkers) in the centre of the fairway; risk/reward tee shot between them and the OB. 2027: championship tee extended, fairway restored left of the…
holes.green: Double green shared with the 2nd; bunkers in front and behind. The front-right pin is about eight paces from the boundary fence. Rises sharply at the front.

holes.name: Road
holes.note: Blind drive over the hotel corner; from the championship tee the carry over the replica shed is about 260 yds (2015).
holes.green: Single green and the smallest on the course (7,078 sq ft). The R&A calls it the shallowest green; 10 yd is its shallowest point.

holes.name: Tom Morris
holes.note: Drivable for long hitters.
holes.green: Single green, the largest single green (15,570 sq ft). Valley of Sin short left; boundary fence just behind.

courses.name: TPC Sawgrass - THE PLAYERS Stadium Course
courses.dataAsOf: TPC Sawgrass Stadium Course scorecard (PDF posted on tpc.com January 2025, still linked from the course page in 2026; no edition date printed). Tournament yardage from THE PLAYERS Championship 2026 (Mar 12-15, 2026), unchanged from 2025.

greens.grass: TifEagle bermudagrass, overseeded with Poa trivialis for THE PLAYERS (regrassed from MiniVerde in the 2016 renovation)
greens.stimp: About 13 for THE PLAYERS (reported for 2025); daily-play speed not published

holes.note: Slight dogleg right with a narrow landing area; trees left, long fairway bunker right.
holes.green: Long, narrow green; large bunkers front and left, grass bunkers front-right, right and behind.

holes.note: Short, reachable par 5; trees both sides. New tournament tee in 2025 took it from 532 to 555 yards.
holes.green: Deep sand and grass bunkers around the green; spectator mounds.
Bunker front, grass bunkers right, large bunker left and back-left. Two tiers, sloping back to front.

holes.note: Short par 4 that demands accuracy.
holes.green: Shallowest green on the course (25-yd depth); small deep bunkers right and behind; spectator mounds behind. Two tiers, very undulating.

holes.note: Dogleg right with a generous landing area; long bunker down the right.
holes.green: Deep, narrow green; grass and sand bunkers, a waste area and palms around it. Rolling.

holes.note: Target-style hole; dense trees right, two fairway bunkers left. New tournament tee in 2025 (393 to 413 yards) and the overhanging tree near the tee was restored.
holes.green: Bunkers and palms around the green. Two tiers; slopes right to left and back to front.

holes.note: Long, slight dogleg right; thick trees right. The tee was moved about 5 yards right when the lake was enlarged.
holes.green: Bunkers front and left. Falls away sharply off the back.

holes.note: Longest par 3 on the course.
holes.green: Deep, narrow green ringed by sand and grass bunkers; open at the front for running shots. Sloping.

holes.note: Longest hole. Woods left affect the second shot. A tee added in the 2016 renovation gives the option of playing it about 20 yards longer.
holes.green: Very thin green; banked bunkers left and behind; spectator mound behind. Slopes steeply from the front to the back right.

holes.note: Dogleg left; large bunker left, dense trees right. 1.
holes.green: Looks large from the fairway but is narrow; two bunkers front-right, grass bunkers left. Falls away from the player.

holes.note: Dense trees and a very large bunker beside the driving area. New tee in 2025 (558 to 573 yards); the left fairway bunker was moved back.
holes.green: Bunker across the front; closely mown run-off on the left.

holes.note: Rebuilt in 2016 as a drivable dogleg-left par 4 (about 302 yards from a forward tee option).
holes.green: Pot bunkers and rough ground right; trees beyond the green for drives that run through. Several tiers; slopes sharply toward the water on the left.
Two small, deep bunkers. Three tiers; the left side drops steeply toward the water.

holes.note: Hardest hole at the 2025 PLAYERS (difficulty rank 1). A large bunker lies between the driving area and the green.
holes.green: Very large green; bunkers front-left, right and behind. Severe undulations and long slopes.

holes.note: Dogleg right; fairway bunker down the right. In 2016 the rough right of the fairway bunker was replaced with trees and natural areas.
holes.green: Large bunker left, small bunker front-right, grass bunkers right and behind.

holes.note: Reachable par 5 and the easiest hole at the 2025 PLAYERS; oak trees block the left. New tee in 2025 (523 to 537 yards).
holes.green: Spectator mound behind the green. Two tiers; slopes left to right toward the water.

holes.note: Often called the Island Green (a nickname, not an official hole name). A drop area sits about 75 yards from the centre of the green. The walkway is in play.
holes.green: 3,912 sq ft, 78 ft deep x 81 ft wide (Golf News Net).

holes.note: Dogleg left; spectator mounds and trees right.
holes.green: Grass bunkers front-right; one bunker left and long; spectator mound behind the green.
